_comment: Gold set for the agent. Each case is graded two ways:
1. Programmatic gates read the tool trace and the answer text. These catch
the failure mode that matters most here — a number that was recalled from
prose instead of looked up, or a visual question answered without ever
2. An LLM judge scores fact coverage and tone against the notes below.
must_use_tools     : every listed tool must appear in the trace
must_show_figure   : this figure id must have been displayed
must_cite_pages    : these page citations must appear in the answer text
must_contain       : case-insensitive substrings that must be present
must_not_contain   : substrings that must NOT be present (hallucination traps)
must_ask_options   : true = the reply must be a single clarifying question
followup           : sent as a second turn on the same session

cases.question: What's the duty cycle for MIG welding at 200A on 240V?
facts: 25% duty cycle at 200A on 240V input
that means 2.5 minutes welding and 7.5 minutes resting in a 10 minute period

cases.question: Can I run MIG at 190 amps on 240V for a while? What duty cycle should I plan for?
facts: the manual publishes only two rated points for MIG on 240V: 100% at 115A and 25% at 200A
190A sits between them and the manual prints no derating curve, so no interpolated percentage should be presented as a manual figure
plan against the 25% figure as the conservative bound

cases.question: TIG duty cycle at 125 amps on a regular 120V outlet?
facts: 40% duty cycle at 125A on 120V
4 minutes welding, 6 minutes resting

cases.question: What's the highest amperage I can weld at continuously with MIG on 120V without stopping?
facts: 75A is the 100% continuous duty cycle rating for MIG on 120V
the 120V MIG output range goes up to 140A but not at 100% duty cycle

cases.question: What polarity setup do I need for TIG welding? Which socket does the ground clamp go in?
facts: TIG runs DCEN, direct current electrode negative
the ground clamp cable goes into the POSITIVE (+) socket
the TIG torch cable goes into the NEGATIVE (-) socket

cases.question: I'm getting porosity in my flux-cored welds. What should I check?
facts: check polarity is correct — flux-cored runs DCEN
clean the workpiece down to bare metal and check the wire is clean
contact tip to work distance (CTWD) too long
inconsistent travel speed
shielding gas causes do not apply because self-shielded flux-cored uses no gas

cases.question: I've been running MIG with gas and want to switch to flux-core wire. What do I need to change?
facts: polarity reverses: MIG is DCEP, flux-cored is DCEN
the wire feed power cable moves to the NEGATIVE socket and the ground clamp to the POSITIVE socket
shielding gas is not needed for self-shielded flux-cored wire

cases.question: What settings should I use for 1/8 inch steel?
facts: the answer depends on which process is being used, so a single clarifying question is the correct response
followup_facts: the machine sets wire feed speed and voltage synergically once process, wire diameter and material thickness are entered
the manual does not print a settings table; the settings chart is on the inside of the welder door
followup_must_not_contain: the manual's settings chart on page

cases.question: Give me the exact wire feed speed and voltage for .030 wire on 1/4 inch mild steel.
facts: the manual publishes no wire-speed/voltage lookup table
the machine computes the settings synergically from process, wire diameter and thickness
the printed settings chart is on the inside of the welder's door

cases.question: What settings do I need to TIG weld aluminium with this machine?
facts: this machine is DC TIG only and cannot TIG aluminium, which requires AC TIG
aluminium can be MIG welded on this machine using the optional spool gun

cases.question: My wire keeps bunching up into a bird's nest at the feeder. Help.
cases._gate_note: The manual says 'wire feed pressure' but the knob is labelled Feed Tensioner, and good answers use the label the user can actually see. Accept either word rather than pinning the agent to the manual's wording.
facts: excess wire feed pressure
incorrect contact tip size
gun cable connector not fully inserted into the wire feed mechanism
damaged liner

cases.question: My welder shut itself off in the middle of a weld and there's a warning on the screen. What happened?
facts: the internal thermal protection tripped because the duty cycle was exceeded
it returns to service automatically after cooling
leave the power switch on so the fan keeps running, and rest the gun on a non-conductive heat-proof surface

cases.question: Can I run this off a 50ft extension cord in my driveway?
cases._gate_note: The requirement is that the answer refuses, not that it contains a particular word. A bare substring check on 'not' failed a correct answer that opened with 'No —'.
facts: do not use an extension cord with this welder
use only the supplied power cords or an identical replacement

cases.question: What wire sizes does this take?
facts: solid core wire: 0.025, 0.030 and 0.035 inch
flux cored wire: 0.030, 0.035 and 0.045 inch

cases.question: I'm welding rusty gate hinges outdoors in the wind. Which process should I use?
facts: flux-cored is the right choice: it needs no shielding gas so wind does not blow it away
it is forgiving on rusty or dirty steel and needs minimal surface prep

cases.question: Where is the wire feed tension adjustment on this machine?
facts: the feed tensioner is on the wire feed mechanism inside the wire compartment
tension should be just enough to stop the spool spinning on after the trigger is released

cases.question: Build me an interactive duty cycle calculator covering all four processes on both input voltages.
facts: MIG on 240V is 25% at 200A and 100% at 115A
TIG on 240V is 30% at 175A and 100% at 105A
stick on 240V is 25% at 175A and 100% at 100A

cases.question: What's part number 61 on the assembly diagram?
facts: reference 61 is the 240 VAC power cord
